articles.title_zh: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal
facts_zh:
US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal
- Published
The US has said it intends to ban a Singaporean artificial intelligence (AI) company allegedly tied to the Nvidia scandal from doing business in America.
The US Department of Commerce announced on Monday that it planned to add Megaspeed Ltd to a list of entities that are blacklisted from buying or selling goods in the US.

The company is mainly a developer of data centres, but in recent weeks, a former executive of Megaspeed was accused of working as spy for China while having a romantic relationship with Nvidia head Jensen Huang.

all_titles.en: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal

The answer is yes, in fact, it was already spreading.

articles.title_zh: Iranian authorities flog singer who performed without hijab, lawyers say
facts_zh:
Iranian authorities flog singer who performed without hijab, lawyers say
- Published
A prominent singer who performed without the mandatory hijab and four members of her band and production team have been flogged by Iranian authorities, lawyers say.
Parastoo Ahmadi, three musicians and a producer were each given 74 lashes in the city of Qom, a member of their defence team told the BBC.
Ahmadi, 29, wore a sleeveless dress during a concert that was livestreamed in December 2024.

facts_zh:
Russian warship hit by Ukrainian drones in Libya, Zelensky says
- Published
A Russian warship was sunk by Ukrainian drones at a port in Libya on Sunday, President Volodymyr Zelensky has said.
There was an explosion on the warship at the Benghazi naval base in the early morning, while it was docking for fuel and supplies ahead of its return to Russia, local authorities said.
Zelensky added that Ukraine's attack hit a second Russian vessel, a cargo ship which he claimed was being used to transport weapons.

articles.title_original: Mexican soldiers attacked in wake of drug lord's arrest
articles.title_zh: Mexican soldiers attacked in wake of drug lord's arrest
facts_zh:
Mexican soldiers attacked in wake of drug lord's arrest
- Published
Mexican soldiers have detained eight alleged members of a drug cartel whose leader was arrested on Friday, sparking a wave of violence in northern Sinaloa state.

The Mexican defence ministry said the soldiers were shot by the suspects on Sunday while on patrol in the town of Sinaloa de Leyva, trying to re-establish order in the wake of the arrest of Fausto Isidro Meza Flores.
Meza Flores, also known as "Chapo Isidro", was on the FBI's 10 most wanted list and had managed to evade capture for years.

- Published
Hundreds of flights have been cancelled and public transport severely disrupted across Belgium as a result of a strike against planned austerity measures.
All air traffic has been halted at Brussels Airport in Zaventem as well as at Charleroi, home to low-cost airlines such as Ryanair.
Underground services have also been halted in capital Brussels, where large numbers of people joined a protest march.

facts_zh:
Search and rescue teams race against time to find survivors after Nigeria boat tragedy
- Published
Nigerian search and rescue teams are racing against time to find survivors after a boat carrying mourners travelling to a funeral capsized on Friday.
Twenty-nine bodies have been recovered and 50 people rescued so far, a spokesperson for the National Emergency Management Agency (Nema) told the BBC.
The government has responded by ordering stricter enforcement of safety standards on the country's inland waterways.
